gaps.sentence: The house ___ badly since the owner emigrated.
The suspect ___ to have left the country.
He refuses ___ (tell) what to do by people he's never met.
gaps.explanation: 'Refuse' takes a to-infinitive; passive meaning needs to be + told.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

gaps.sentence: Every complaint ___ (investigate) since the new ombudsman took over.
gaps.explanation: 'Every complaint' is singular, so present perfect passive: has been + investigated.

gaps.sentence: The letters ___ by the time I arrived at the office.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive: the sending preceded the arrival.

gaps.sentence: Construction ___ (halt) after the discovery of Roman remains.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: was + halted. The halting authority is unnamed.
